title: Icon Briefly Jumps back to Original Position when Dragged Across Monitors.
line: Dragging a desktop icon to another screen no longer makes it flash back at its old spot before it appears where it was dropped.
explanation: All screens show the same Desktop folder, and each screen's view filters items by the screen they are mapped to. When an icon was dropped on another screen, the drop handler changed its mapping but only announced it through ScreenMapper's 100 ms compression timer; meanwhile the drag ended on the source screen and un-blanked the icon, so it was drawn at its old place until the timer fired and the views were re-filtered. The drop now announces the mapping change immediately (once, for the last dropped item), so the source view removes the icon and the target view shows it before the drag ends.

commits.message:
folder: update all desktops right away when moving icons between screens

When icons were dropped on another screen, their new screen was only
announced after a 100 ms delay, so the source screen briefly showed them
again at their old place. The mapping change is now sent immediately.

BUG: 482572

media.caption: Master, frames every 40 ms around the drop: the icon comes back at its old spot on the left screen for ~120 ms, and appears on the right screen only after ~160 ms.
With the fix: the left screen stays empty and the icon shows on the right screen within 40 ms.
Both screens, 4x slower, master: watch the top-left corner right after the drop.
Same drag with the fix: no flash on the left screen.

review.text: Good root-cause diagnosis and effective visual fix—announcing the cross-screen ScreenMapper change immediately eliminates the post-drop flash on the source monitor. However, triggering invalidateFilterIfComplete() synchronously during drag->exec() removes the dragged rows from the source FolderModel while FolderModel::dragSelectedInternal() still holds non-persistent QModelIndex entries in m_dragIndexes, causing lines 1270-1276 to emit dataChanged(first, last, {BlankRole}) with stale/out-of-bounds indexes on every cross-screen drop (and risking BlankRole matching a shifted remaining item during unwind).
changes: Make m_dragIndexes safe against rows being filtered out during drag->exec() (for example, store QPersistentModelIndex entries in m_dragIndexes and only emit dataChanged for still-valid indexes after drag->exec() returns).

In the drop loop in FolderModel::drop(), determine the last item by index rather than value comparison (url == urls.constLast()) in case of duplicate URLs, and call removeItemFromDisabledScreen() before triggering addMapping() with ScreenMapper::ImmediateSignal.

reviews.text: Good root-cause diagnosis and effective visual fix—announcing the cross-screen ScreenMapper change immediately eliminates the post-drop flash on the source monitor. However, triggering invalidateFilterIfComplete() synchronously during drag->exec() removes the dragged rows from the source FolderModel while FolderModel::dragSelectedInternal() still holds non-persistent QModelIndex entries in m_dragIndexes, causing lines 1270-1276 to emit dataChanged(first, last, {BlankRole}) with stale/out-of-bounds indexes on every cross-screen drop (and risking BlankRole matching a shifted remaining item during unwind).
changes: Make m_dragIndexes safe against rows being filtered out during drag->exec() (for example, store QPersistentModelIndex entries in m_dragIndexes and only emit dataChanged for still-valid indexes after drag->exec() returns).

In the drop loop in FolderModel::drop(), determine the last item by index rather than value comparison (url == urls.constLast()) in case of duplicate URLs, and call removeItemFromDisabledScreen() before triggering addMapping() with ScreenMapper::ImmediateSignal.

reviews.text: This is the real cause: the cross-screen drop updated the ScreenMapper only through its 100 ms compression timer, so the source view un-blanked the icon at its old cell before it was filtered out. Emitting the mapping change immediately for the last dropped URL keeps the compression for multi-item drops and fixes the flash with a minimal change in the right place (foldermodel.cpp). The frame sheets clearly show the icon at its old cell on the left screen for 40-120 ms before the fix and never after, and the icon lands at the same spot on the right screen. Multi-icon drags, dragging back and moving within one screen were checked; the second, delayed signal is redundant but harmless.
